sanskrit: carmaṇvatīṃ samāsādya niyato niyatāśanaḥ rantidevābhyanujñāto agniṣṭomaphalaṃ labhet
english: Reaching the Carmaṇvatī river, self-controlled and abstemious, with the blessing of Rantideva one obtains the fruit of the Agniṣṭoma sacrifice.

sanskrit: tato gaccheta dharmajña himavatsutam arbudam pṛthivyāṃ yatra vai chidraṃ pūrvam āsīd yudhiṣṭhira
english: Then, O knower of dharma, one should go to Arbuda, the son of the Himālayas, where, O Yudhiṣṭhira, a cleft in the earth once existed in ancient times.

sanskrit: tatrāśramo vasiṣṭhasya triṣu lokeṣu viśrutaḥ tatroṣya rajanīm ekāṃ gosahasraphalaṃ labhet
english: There stands the hermitage of Vasiṣṭha, renowned throughout the three worlds; by spending a single night there one obtains the merit of gifting a thousand cows.

sanskrit: piṅgātīrtham upaspṛśya brahmacārī jitendriyaḥ kapilānāṃ naravyāghra śatasya phalam aśnute
english: By bathing at the Pinga tirtha, O tiger among men, a celibate who has conquered his senses obtains the merit of gifting a hundred tawny cows.

sanskrit: tato gaccheta dharmajña prabhāsaṃ lokaviśrutam yatra saṃnihito nityaṃ svayam eva hutāśanaḥ devatānāṃ mukhaṃ vīra analo 'nilasārathiḥ
english: Then, O knower of dharma, one should go to Prabhāsa, renowned throughout the world, where Agni himself, the mouth of the gods and charioteer of the wind, is ever present, O hero.

sanskrit: tasmiṃs tīrthavare snātvā śuciḥ prayatamānasaḥ agniṣṭomātirātrābhyāṃ phalaṃ prāpnoti mānavaḥ
english: By bathing at that excellent tirtha, pure and with a composed mind, a man obtains the combined fruit of the Agniṣṭoma and Atirātra sacrifices.

sanskrit: tato gatvā sarasvatyāḥ sāgarasya ca saṃgame gosahasraphalaṃ prāpya svargaloke mahīyate dīpyamāno 'gnivan nityaṃ prabhayā bharatarṣabha
english: Then, going to the confluence of the Sarasvatī and the ocean, one obtains the merit of a thousand cows and is honored in the heavenly world, blazing perpetually with radiance like fire, O bull of the Bharatas.

sanskrit: trirātram uṣitas tatra tarpayet pitṛdevatāḥ prabhāsate yathā somo aśvamedhaṃ ca vindati
english: Dwelling there for three nights and gratifying the ancestors and the gods, one shines like the moon and obtains the fruit of the Aśvamedha sacrifice.

sanskrit: varadānaṃ tato gacchet tīrthaṃ bharatasattama viṣṇor durvāsasā yatra varo datto yudhiṣṭhira
english: Then one should go to the tirtha called Varadana, O best of the Bharatas, where a boon was granted to Viṣṇu by Durvasa, O Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: varadāne naraḥ snātvā gosahasraphalaṃ labhet tato dvāravatīṃ gacchen niyato niyatāśanaḥ piṇḍārake naraḥ snātvā labhed bahu suvarṇakam
english: By bathing at Varadana a man obtains the merit of a thousand cows. Then one should go to Dvāravatī, self-controlled and abstemious; by bathing at Piṇḍāraka a man obtains abundant gold.

sanskrit: tasmiṃs tīrthe mahābhāga padmalakṣaṇalakṣitāḥ adyāpi mudrā dṛśyante tad adbhutam ariṃdama
english: At that tirtha, O greatly fortunate one, marks bearing the signs of the lotus are visible even today — that is wondrous, O slayer of foes.

sanskrit: triśūlāṅkāni padmāni dṛśyante kurunandana mahādevasya sāṃnidhyaṃ tatraiva bharatarṣabha
english: Lotuses marked with the trident are seen there, O joy of the Kurus; the presence of Mahādeva is there indeed, O bull of the Bharatas.

sanskrit: sāgarasya ca sindhoś ca saṃgamaṃ prāpya bhārata tīrthe salilarājasya snātvā prayatamānasaḥ
english: Reaching the confluence of the ocean and the Sindhu river, O Bharata, and bathing at the tirtha of the lord of waters with a composed mind —

sanskrit: tarpayitvā pitṝn devān ṛṣīṃś ca bharatarṣabha prāpnoti vāruṇaṃ lokaṃ dīpyamānaḥ svatejasā
english: — and having gratified the ancestors, the gods, and the sages, O bull of the Bharatas, one attains the world of Varuṇa, blazing with one's own splendor.

sanskrit: śaṅkukarṇeśvaraṃ devam arcayitvā yudhiṣṭhira aśvamedhaṃ daśaguṇaṃ pravadanti manīṣiṇaḥ
english: By worshipping the god Shankukarneshvara, O Yudhiṣṭhira, the wise declare one obtains tenfold the fruit of the Aśvamedha sacrifice.

sanskrit: pradakṣiṇam upāvṛtya gaccheta bharatarṣabha tīrthaṃ kuruvaraśreṣṭha triṣu lokeṣu viśrutam dṛmīti nāmnā vikhyātaṃ sarvapāpapramocanam
english: Having circumambulated it, one should proceed, O bull of the Bharatas, O best among the excellent Kurus, to the tirtha renowned throughout the three worlds, known by the name Drimi, which liberates one from all sins.

sanskrit: yatra brahmādayo devā upāsante maheśvaram tatra snātvārcayitvā ca rudraṃ devagaṇair vṛtam janmaprabhṛti pāpāni kṛtāni nudate naraḥ
english: Where Brahmā and the other gods worship Maheśvara — there, by bathing and worshipping Rudra surrounded by his divine hosts, a man destroys the sins committed from birth.

sanskrit: dṛmī cātra naraśreṣṭha sarvadevair abhiṣṭutā tatra snātvā naravyāghra hayamedham avāpnuyāt
english: And here Drimi, O best of men, is praised by all the gods; by bathing there, O tiger among men, one obtains the fruit of the Hayamedha sacrifice.

sanskrit: jitvā yatra mahāprājña viṣṇunā prabhaviṣṇunā purā śaucaṃ kṛtaṃ rājan hatvā daivatakaṇṭakān
english: Where the all-powerful Viṣṇu, of great wisdom, O king, having conquered and slain those who were thorns to the gods, performed purification in ancient times —

sanskrit: tato gaccheta dharmajña vasor dhārām abhiṣṭutām gamanād eva tasyāṃ hi hayamedham avāpnuyāt
english: — then one should go, O knower of dharma, to the celebrated Vashodhara; by the mere act of going there one obtains the fruit of the Hayamedha sacrifice.

sanskrit: snātvā kuruvaraśreṣṭha prayatātmā tu mānavaḥ tarpya devān pitṝṃś caiva viṣṇuloke mahīyate
english: Having bathed there, O best among the excellent Kurus, with a purified soul, and having gratified the gods and the ancestors, a man is honored in the world of Viṣṇu.

sanskrit: tīrthaṃ cātra paraṃ puṇyaṃ vasūnāṃ bharatarṣabha tatra snātvā ca pītvā ca vasūnāṃ saṃmato bhavet
english: And here there is a supremely holy tirtha of the Vasus, O bull of the Bharatas; by bathing and drinking the waters there, one becomes honored among the Vasus.

sanskrit: sindhūttamam iti khyātaṃ sarvapāpapraṇāśanam tatra snātvā naraśreṣṭha labhed bahu suvarṇakam
english: Known as Sindhuttama, the destroyer of all sins — by bathing there, O best of men, one obtains abundant gold.

sanskrit: brahmatuṅgaṃ samāsādya śuciḥ prayatamānasaḥ brahmalokam avāpnoti sukṛtī virajā naraḥ
english: Reaching Brahmatunga, pure and with composed mind, a meritorious and stainless man attains the world of Brahmā.

sanskrit: kumārikāṇāṃ śakrasya tīrthaṃ siddhaniṣevitam tatra snātvā naraḥ kṣipraṃ śakralokam avāpnuyāt
english: At the tirtha of Śakra's maidens, frequented by the Siddhas — by bathing there a man swiftly attains the world of Śakra.

sanskrit: reṇukāyāś ca tatraiva tīrthaṃ devaniṣevitam tatra snātvā bhaved vipro vimalaś candramā yathā
english: And there also is the tirtha of Renuka, frequented by the gods; by bathing there a brahmin becomes as spotless as the moon.

sanskrit: atha pañcanadaṃ gatvā niyato niyatāśanaḥ pañca yajñān avāpnoti kramaśo ye 'nukīrtitāḥ
english: Then, going to Pañcanada, self-controlled and abstemious, one obtains in succession the five sacrifices that have been enumerated.

sanskrit: tato gaccheta dharmajña bhīmāyāḥ sthānam uttamam tatra snātvā tu yonyāṃ vai naro bharatasattama
english: Then one should go, O knower of dharma, to the excellent abode of Bhīma; by bathing there at the womb-shaped place, O best of the Bharatas —

sanskrit: devyāḥ putro bhaved rājaṃs taptakuṇḍalavigrahaḥ gavāṃ śatasahasrasya phalaṃ caivāpnuyān mahat
english: — a man becomes as if a son of the goddess, with a form adorned with glowing earrings, O king, and obtains the great merit of a hundred thousand cows.

sanskrit: girimuñjaṃ samāsādya triṣu lokeṣu viśrutam pitāmahaṃ namaskṛtya gosahasraphalaṃ labhet
english: Reaching Girimunjha, renowned throughout the three worlds, and bowing to the Grandfather Brahmā, one obtains the merit of a thousand cows.

sanskrit: tato gaccheta dharmajña vimalaṃ tīrtham uttamam adyāpi yatra dṛśyante matsyāḥ sauvarṇarājatāḥ
english: Then one should go, O knower of dharma, to the excellent and pure tirtha where even today fish of gold and silver are seen.

sanskrit: tatra snātvā naraśreṣṭha vājapeyam avāpnuyāt sarvapāpaviśuddhātmā gacchec ca paramāṃ gatim
english: By bathing there, O best of men, one obtains the fruit of the Vājapeya sacrifice; with a soul purified of all sins, one attains the highest state.

sanskrit: tato gaccheta maladāṃ triṣu lokeṣu viśrutām paścimāyāṃ tu saṃdhyāyām upaspṛśya yathāvidhi
english: Then one should go to Malada, renowned throughout the three worlds, and at the western twilight touch its waters according to the prescribed rites.

sanskrit: caruṃ narendra saptārcer yathāśakti nivedayet pitṝṇām akṣayaṃ dānaṃ pravadanti manīṣiṇaḥ
english: One should offer oblation to the seven-flamed fire according to one's ability, O king of men; the wise declare this to be an inexhaustible gift to the ancestors.

sanskrit: gavāṃ śatasahasreṇa rājasūyaśatena ca aśvamedhasahasreṇa śreyān saptārciṣaś caruḥ
english: The oblation to the seven-flamed fire is superior to the gift of a hundred thousand cows, to a hundred Rājasūya sacrifices, and to a thousand Aśvamedha sacrifices.

sanskrit: tato nivṛtto rājendra vastrāpadam athāviśet abhigamya mahādevam aśvamedhaphalaṃ labhet
english: Then, returning, O king of kings, one should enter Vastraapada; having approached Mahādeva there, one obtains the fruit of the Aśvamedha sacrifice.

sanskrit: maṇimantaṃ samāsādya brahmacārī samāhitaḥ ekarātroṣito rājann agniṣṭomaphalaṃ labhet
english: Reaching Manimanta, a celibate with a composed mind, having spent a single night there, O king, obtains the fruit of the Agniṣṭoma sacrifice.

sanskrit: atha gaccheta rājendra devikāṃ lokaviśrutām prasūtir yatra viprāṇāṃ śrūyate bharatarṣabha
english: Then one should go, O king of kings, to the world-renowned Devikā, where the origin of the brahmins is said to have occurred, O bull of the Bharatas.

sanskrit: triśūlapāṇeḥ sthānaṃ ca triṣu lokeṣu viśrutam devikāyāṃ naraḥ snātvā samabhyarcya maheśvaram
english: And there is the abode of the trident-bearing one, renowned throughout the three worlds; bathing in the Devikā and duly worshipping Maheśvara —

sanskrit: yathāśakti caruṃ tatra nivedya bharatarṣabha sarvakāmasamṛddhasya yajñasya labhate phalam
english: — and offering oblation there according to one's ability, O bull of the Bharatas, one obtains the fruit of a sacrifice that fulfills all desires.

sanskrit: kāmākhyaṃ tatra rudrasya tīrthaṃ devarṣisevitam tatra snātvā naraḥ kṣipraṃ siddhim āpnoti bhārata
english: There is the tirtha of Rudra called Kamakhya, frequented by divine sages; by bathing there a man swiftly attains perfection, O Bharata.

sanskrit: yajanaṃ yājanaṃ gatvā tathaiva brahmavālukām puṣpanyāsa upaspṛśya na śocen maraṇaṃ tataḥ
english: Going to Yajanam and Yajanam and likewise to Brahmavaluka, and touching the water at Pushpanyasa, one need not grieve at death thereafter.

sanskrit: ardhayojanavistārāṃ pañcayojanam āyatām etāvad devikām āhuḥ puṇyāṃ devarṣisevitām
english: Half a yojana wide and five yojanas long — such is the extent of the holy Devikā, frequented by divine sages.

sanskrit: tato gaccheta dharmajña dīrghasatraṃ yathākramam yatra brahmādayo devāḥ siddhāś ca paramarṣayaḥ dīrghasatram upāsante dakṣiṇābhir yatavratāḥ
english: Then one should go, O knower of dharma, to Dirghasatra in proper order, where Brahmā and the other gods, the Siddhas and the great sages, perform the long Dirghasatra sacrifice with ritual gifts, observing their vows.

sanskrit: gamanād eva rājendra dīrghasatram ariṃdama rājasūyāśvamedhābhyāṃ phalaṃ prāpnoti mānavaḥ
english: By the mere act of going to Dirghasatra, O king of kings, O slayer of foes, a man obtains the combined fruit of the Rājasūya and Aśvamedha sacrifices.

sanskrit: tato vinaśanaṃ gacchen niyato niyatāśanaḥ gacchaty antarhitā yatra marupṛṣṭhe sarasvatī camase ca śivodbhede nāgodbhede ca dṛśyate
english: Then one should go to Vinashana, self-controlled and abstemious, where the Sarasvatī disappears into the desert surface, but reappears at Chamasa, at Shivodbheda, and at Nagodbheda.

sanskrit: snātvā ca camasodbhede agniṣṭomaphalaṃ labhet śivodbhede naraḥ snātvā gosahasraphalaṃ labhet
english: By bathing at Camasodbheda one obtains the fruit of the Agniṣṭoma sacrifice; by bathing at Shivodbheda a man obtains the merit of a thousand cows.

sanskrit: nāgodbhede naraḥ snātvā nāgalokam avāpnuyāt śaśayānaṃ ca rājendra tīrtham āsādya durlabham śaśarūpapraticchannāḥ puṣkarā yatra bhārata
english: By bathing at Nagodbheda a man attains the world of the serpents; and reaching the tirtha called Shashayanu, which is difficult to attain, O king of kings, where the lotus ponds are covered in the form of hares, O Bharata —

sanskrit: sarasvatyāṃ mahārāja anu saṃvatsaraṃ hi te snāyante bharataśreṣṭha vṛttāṃ vai kārttikīṃ sadā
english: — on the Sarasvatī, O great king, they bathe every year throughout the year, O best of the Bharatas, always on the Kartika full-moon day.

sanskrit: tatra snātvā naravyāghra dyotate śaśivat sadā gosahasraphalaṃ caiva prāpnuyād bharatarṣabha
english: By bathing there, O tiger among men, one shines forever like the moon, and obtains the merit of a thousand cows, O bull of the Bharatas.

sanskrit: kumārakoṭim āsādya niyataḥ kurunandana tatrābhiṣekaṃ kurvīta pitṛdevārcane rataḥ gavāmayam avāpnoti kulaṃ caiva samuddharet
english: Reaching Kumarakoti, self-controlled, O joy of the Kurus, one should perform the ablution there, devoted to the worship of ancestors and gods; one obtains the fruit of the cow-sacrifice and also elevates one's lineage.

sanskrit: tato gaccheta dharmajña rudrakoṭiṃ samāhitaḥ purā yatra mahārāja ṛṣikoṭiḥ samāhitā praharṣeṇa ca saṃviṣṭā devadarśanakāṅkṣayā
english: Then one should go, O knower of dharma, to Rudrakoti with a composed mind, where, O great king, a crore of sages once assembled, filled with joy, longing for the vision of the god.

sanskrit: ahaṃ pūrvam ahaṃ pūrvaṃ drakṣyāmi vṛṣabhadhvajam evaṃ saṃprasthitā rājann ṛṣayaḥ kila bhārata
english: "I first, I first shall see him of the bull-banner" — thus the sages set out, O king, O Bharata.

sanskrit: tato yogeṣvareṇāpi yogam āsthāya bhūpate teṣāṃ manyupraṇāśārtham ṛṣīṇāṃ bhāvitātmanām
english: Then even the Lord of Yoga, O master of the earth, assuming his yoga form, in order to remove the anger of those sages of cultivated souls —

sanskrit: sṛṣṭā koṭis tu rudrāṇām ṛṣīṇām agrataḥ sthitā mayā pūrvataraṃ dṛṣṭa iti te menire pṛthak
english: — created a crore of Rudras who stood before the sages, so that each one thought separately: "I have seen him before the others."

sanskrit: teṣāṃ tuṣṭo mahādeva ṛṣīṇām ugratejasām bhaktyā paramayā rājan varaṃ teṣāṃ pradiṣṭavān adya prabhṛti yuṣmākaṃ dharmavṛddhir bhaviṣyati
english: Mahādeva, pleased with those sages of fierce splendor, by their supreme devotion, O king, granted them a boon: "From this day forward, your dharma shall ever increase."

sanskrit: tatra snātvā naravyāghra rudrakoṭyāṃ naraḥ śuciḥ aśvamedham avāpnoti kulaṃ caiva samuddharet
english: By bathing there, O tiger among men, at Rudrakoti, a pure man obtains the fruit of the Aśvamedha sacrifice and elevates his lineage as well.

sanskrit: tato gaccheta rājendra saṃgamaṃ lokaviśrutam sarasvatyā mahāpuṇyam upāsante janārdanam
english: Then one should go, O king of kings, to the Sangama, renowned throughout the world, supremely holy on the Sarasvatī, where Janārdana is worshipped.

sanskrit: yatra brahmādayo devā ṛṣayaḥ siddhacāraṇāḥ abhigacchanti rājendra caitraśuklacaturdaśīm
english: Where Brahmā and the other gods, sages, Siddhas and Cāraṇas come, O king of kings, on the fourteenth day of the bright fortnight of Caitra.

sanskrit: tatra snātvā naravyāghra vinded bahu suvarṇakam sarvapāpaviśuddhātmā brahmalokaṃ ca gacchati
english: By bathing there, O tiger among men, one obtains abundant gold; with a soul purified of all sins, one goes to the world of Brahmā.

sanskrit: ṛṣīṇāṃ yatra satrāṇi samāptāni narādhipa satrāvasānam āsādya gosahasraphalaṃ labhet
english: Where the sacrificial sessions of the sages were completed, O lord of men — reaching Satravashana, one obtains the merit of a thousand cows.

sanskrit: pulastya uvāca tato gaccheta rājendra kurukṣetram abhiṣṭutam pāpebhyo vipramucyante tadgatāḥ sarvajantavaḥ
english: Pulastya said: Then one should go, O king of kings, to the celebrated Kurukṣetra; all living beings who go there are freed from their sins.

sanskrit: kurukṣetraṃ gamiṣyāmi kurukṣetre vasāmy aham ya evaṃ satataṃ brūyāt so 'pi pāpaiḥ pramucyate
english: "I shall go to Kurukṣetra, I dwell at Kurukṣetra" — even one who constantly says this is freed from sins.

sanskrit: tatra māsaṃ vased vīra sarasvatyāṃ yudhiṣṭhira yatra brahmādayo devā ṛṣayaḥ siddhacāraṇāḥ
english: One should dwell there for a month on the Sarasvatī, O hero, O Yudhiṣṭhira, where Brahmā and the other gods, sages, Siddhas and Cāraṇas —

sanskrit: gandharvāpsaraso yakṣāḥ pannagāś ca mahīpate brahmakṣetraṃ mahāpuṇyam abhigacchanti bhārata
english: — Gandharvas, Apsaras, Yakṣas and serpents, O lord of the earth, visit the supremely holy Brahmakshetra, O Bharata.

sanskrit: manasāpy abhikāmasya kurukṣetraṃ yudhiṣṭhira pāpāni vipraṇaśyanti brahmalokaṃ ca gacchati
english: Even for one who merely desires Kurukṣetra in mind, O Yudhiṣṭhira, sins are utterly destroyed and one goes to the world of Brahmā.

sanskrit: gatvā hi śraddhayā yuktaḥ kurukṣetraṃ kurūdvaha rājasūyāśvamedhābhyāṃ phalaṃ prāpnoti mānavaḥ
english: Indeed, going to Kurukṣetra with faith, O chief of the Kurus, a man obtains the combined fruit of the Rājasūya and Aśvamedha sacrifices.

sanskrit: tato macakrukaṃ rājan dvārapālaṃ mahābalam yakṣaṃ samabhivādyaiva gosahasraphalaṃ labhet
english: Then, by duly saluting Machacruka, O king, the mighty Yakṣa who is the gatekeeper, one obtains the merit of a thousand cows.

sanskrit: tato gaccheta dharmajña viṣṇoḥ sthānam anuttamam satataṃ nāma rājendra yatra saṃnihito hariḥ
english: Then one should go, O knower of dharma, to the incomparable abode of Viṣṇu called Satatam, O king of kings, where Hari is ever present.

sanskrit: tatra snātvārcayitvā ca trilokaprabhavaṃ harim aśvamedham avāpnoti viṣṇulokaṃ ca gacchati
english: By bathing there and worshipping Hari, the origin of the three worlds, one obtains the fruit of the Aśvamedha sacrifice and goes to the world of Viṣṇu.

sanskrit: tataḥ pāriplavaṃ gacchet tīrthaṃ trailokyaviśrutam agniṣṭomātirātrābhyāṃ phalaṃ prāpnoti mānavaḥ
english: Then one should go to Pariplavama, the tirtha renowned throughout the three worlds; a man obtains the combined fruit of the Agniṣṭoma and Atirātra sacrifices.

sanskrit: pṛthivyās tīrtham āsādya gosahasraphalaṃ labhet tataḥ śālūkinīṃ gatvā tīrthasevī narādhipa daśāśvamedhike snātvā tad eva labhate phalam
english: Reaching the tirtha of the earth, one obtains the merit of a thousand cows. Then, going to Shalukinim, O lord of men, a devotee of tirthas, by bathing at Dashasvamedha obtains that same fruit.

sanskrit: sarpadarvīṃ samāsādya nāgānāṃ tīrtham uttamam agniṣṭomam avāpnoti nāgalokaṃ ca vindati
english: Reaching Sarpadarvi, the excellent tirtha of the serpents, one obtains the fruit of the Agniṣṭoma sacrifice and attains the world of the serpents.

sanskrit: tato gaccheta dharmajña dvārapālaṃ tarantukam tatroṣya rajanīm ekāṃ gosahasraphalaṃ labhet
english: Then one should go, O knower of dharma, to Tarantuka the gatekeeper; by spending a single night there one obtains the merit of a thousand cows.

sanskrit: tataḥ pañcanadaṃ gatvā niyato niyatāśanaḥ koṭitīrtham upaspṛśya hayamedhaphalaṃ labhet aśvinos tīrtham āsādya rūpavān abhijāyate
english: Then, going to Pañcanada, self-controlled and abstemious, by touching the waters of Koṭitīrtha one obtains the fruit of the Hayamedha sacrifice; reaching the tirtha of the Aśvins, one is born with great beauty.

sanskrit: tato gaccheta dharmajña vārāhaṃ tīrtham uttamam viṣṇur vārāharūpeṇa pūrvaṃ yatra sthito 'bhavat tatra snātvā naravyāghra agniṣṭomaphalaṃ labhet
english: Then one should go, O knower of dharma, to the excellent Varaha tirtha, where Viṣṇu formerly stood in the form of the boar; by bathing there, O tiger among men, one obtains the fruit of the Agniṣṭoma sacrifice.

sanskrit: tato jayantyā rājendra somatīrthaṃ samāviśet snātvā phalam avāpnoti rājasūyasya mānavaḥ
english: Then from Jayanti, O king of kings, one should enter the Somatirtha; by bathing there a man obtains the fruit of the Rājasūya sacrifice.

sanskrit: ekahaṃse naraḥ snātvā gosahasraphalaṃ labhet kṛtaśaucaṃ samāsādya tīrthasevī kurūdvaha puṇḍarīkam avāpnoti kṛtaśauco bhaven naraḥ
english: By bathing at Ekahansa a man obtains the merit of a thousand cows; reaching Kritashauca, a devotee of tirthas, O chief of the Kurus, obtains the Pundarika sacrifice and becomes purified.

sanskrit: tato muñjavaṭaṃ nāma mahādevasya dhīmataḥ tatroṣya rajanīm ekāṃ gāṇapatyam avāpnuyāt
english: Then at the place called Munjavata of the wise Mahādeva, by spending a single night there one obtains the lordship of the Ganas.

sanskrit: tatraiva ca mahārāja yakṣī lokapariśrutā tāṃ cābhigamya rājendra puṇyāṃl lokān avāpnuyāt
english: And there too, O great king, dwells a Yakshi renowned throughout the world; by approaching her, O king of kings, one attains the holy worlds.
